quotes.text: AI mistakes on the battlefield have the potential to be catastrophic: civilian casualties, friendly fire, unintended escalation, and calculations made on faulty data. These aren't risks worth taking – not when they can result in unnecessary lives lost or war.

It's important for our laws to keep up with emerging AI developments. So while I'm glad tech companies are engaging on this, we can't depend on them to always do the right thing. We still need regulation to address AI risks and protect people's rights.
https://t.co/rsIgD93Znm

It's so important that the world comes together to establish guardrails for AI to manage risks and ensure this technology strengthens democracy and upholds human rights. It was great to join @AmbUNReform and other leaders at UNGA to discuss the future of AI and global governance. https://t.co/u9pXAvd0Mo

This week, @SenMarkey and I urged @VP to push the importance of civil rights and democratic values at the UK AI Safety Summit – and we’re so glad that she followed through in highlighting these principles and adopting an inclusive definition of AI safety. https://t.co/b14MNTOGTC

It was an honor to speak at the Athens Roundtable this week to discuss AI global governance, including how we can work together internationally, address gaps as AI evolves, and ensure more voices from civil society and the Global South are at the table. https://t.co/neKNStuYBz

AI should never have the final say in deploying nuclear weapons, which pose one of the biggest threats to human life. We've seen that AI consistently makes more aggressive and escalatory decisions than humans in war game simulations, including launching nuclear weapons.

I’m glad to see the FCC take this important step to address AI’s current threats to democracy, but we need to do so much more to establish both national and global guardrails to ensure the responsible and ethical implementation of AI across all areas of life. https://t.co/ItEnAVjeZH

I’m so proud to serve on the Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence so we can expand access to the opportunities created by AI, address challenges and risks, and set up the necessary guardrails to prioritize fairness and human rights. https://t.co/SxZ5cM7dPW
Is there anything put in place to ensure that AI drones do not accidentally target innocent civilians during military operations?
And one of the things we have been hearing a lot of concern about is around AI drones, particularly ones using facial recognition, used during military operations.

So great to join the San Diego Regional Chamber of Commerce’s fireside chat on AI! AI has been a net job creator in San Diego and that's why I’m working to ensure there are guardrails that encourage innovation and growth while also protecting our safety and civil rights. https://t.co/K9y7quvHxJ

Global internet freedom has declined for 13 consecutive years, especially with the increased use of AI. That’s why we need to pass my bipartisan Global Internet Freedom Act to reinforce that internet freedom is fundamental to human rights. https://t.co/Jd2T8zrJzb

the accuracy level you need on AI for something commercial is very different than the accuracy level you need if you are using an AI technology to do a kinetic strike, right? Because then we need, like, 100 percent accuracy. We don't really have a lot of room for error in a way that you might in a commercial system. [...] how should we be thinking about the way, then, to take commercially-produced innovations and figure out how to bring them into DoD, which is a completely different problem set than the way most of these acquisition processes have been designed?

So proud to bring home $1.9 million for @UCSanDiego to help prevent and address wildfires using AI! This technology will help protect our environment, homes, and small businesses and keep us safe. https://t.co/3KyKd0oxmi

We need to address the risks posed by AI in all aspects of life – including in the music industry. So I was glad to speak with Brandon from the Recording Academy and Jolie from Garfield High School on Music Advocacy Day to figure out how we can help support artists. https://t.co/0iceI1cQAk

One reason I ran for Congress was to ensure we're keeping up with challenges like emerging tech. I’m proud of the wins I secured in the Bipartisan AI Task Force's report from AI global governance to empowering sectoral regulators to preventing AI from launching nuclear weapons. https://t.co/g9GvNJMIc4

@dogeai_gov Looks like your AI needs a little work. Congress *could* abolish USAID, but hasn't passed H.R. 5108. That means Donald Trump and Elon Musk can't skirt the law and get rid of it on their own.
It was great to meet the team at Brain Corp, a San Diego-based company developing cutting-edge robotic AI products. https://t.co/FXFto4cd3J

Our federal agencies are struggling to recruit and retain the AI talent we need to serve and protect the American people. That’s why I introduced the bipartisan and bicameral AI Talent Act to change that. 
https://t.co/7P5yZzooJp

The rise of AI is making Jewish people actively less safe so I’m proud to introduce a bipartisan resolution so we can ensure that AI is not a vehicle for antisemitism.
https://t.co/MIFHG4SHXL

The AI competition won't only be won by whoever builds the most powerful model first. Being first won't matter if no one uses what you build—or if you lose control of the technology. The real strategic advantage belongs to the country whose systems the world adopts and builds on.

At the frontier model level, voluntary promises aren't enough. [...] Congress should give a federal regulator the authority, staff, and funding to set and enforce minimum safety standards for companies building the most capable models, while preserving stronger state protections.

For example, we tax labor at a higher rate than capital, which creates a built-in financial incentive for companies to replace human labor with automation and AI. I don't think that's the outcome most Americans want. So we need to tax capital the same as labor and find innovative ways to tax AI usage.

Federal inaction and the lack of strong guardrails for AI systems are making women and children less safe online. Companies have proven they can’t or won’t do the right thing so Congress needs to set guardrails for AI to protect people’s rights and safety.
https://t.co/GVSYF8f0UI

The Pentagon’s move to bring Grok into its classified systems, while pressuring Anthropic to drop key safeguards, is deeply alarming. Undermining AI safety and civil liberties protections could cause large-scale harm. We can’t let this happen.
https://t.co/gW2BDwC1aU

We need strict guardrails when the military uses AI, whether it’s in Iran or anywhere else – full stop.
https://t.co/fWlngriF7e

Trump’s AI framework is a joke and it’s clearly written by his Big Tech donors. We SHOULD have real federal guardrails on AI (but this is far from it), and in the absence of that, states like CA should be able to keep protecting people’s rights and safety.
https://t.co/pOBMOHYCDx

Section 702 of FISA has allowed the government to spy on the American people for decades – but the rise of AI makes it a lot easier and faster. We can’t let this practice continue unchecked, so I’m still a hard NO on a clean FISA reauthorization.
https://t.co/svLewFepjn
I just introduced the most ambitious and practical AI governance bill in American history. https://t.co/MgtY0aN4pa

Federal laws shouldn't become optional just because technology is new. AI is already helping make life-altering decisions for millions of Americans -- whether they get a loan, a job, or health care coverage -- but too often, it's operating in a gray area.

Congress has been too slow on AI. My approach protects states’ progress and helps federal agencies hold companies accountable when AI is used to break existing federal laws.

My bill won't solve every concern with AI, but it would be a big step forward. https://t.co/iS3DHl3GMn

It was great to tour AiCella & Invetech and see how they’re using AI to make lifesaving cell therapies faster, cheaper, and made in San Diego! This is what American biomanufacturing and responsible use of AI can look like. https://t.co/zImj609YUW

I visited UCSD’s Supercomputer Center to learn more about how they’re using advanced computing and AI to tackle real-world challenges, including supporting wildfire response and advancing health care research.

It’s critical that we harness AI to help people, not just a few tech companies.

Congress needs to make sure that the AI transition happens equitably and big corporations don’t reap all the benefits. That’s why @RepCasar, @ValerieFoushee, and I introduced a bill to tax AI companies and help workers left behind by the AI transition.
https://t.co/oF8PAPEr7M

The Pentagon is racing to adopt AI like most other workplaces, but when AI fails at the Pentagon, the consequences can be deadly and could even pull the United States into a war. That's why we need a department-wide program to catch and fix AI incidents and vulnerabilities before they turn into catastrophes.
We don’t have time to wait. The massive threats posed by AI are here and now, and Congress needs to act. https://t.co/AEh3WcXJII

We’re seeing more warnings about the potentially catastrophic risks of AI from bioweapons to nuclear threats. That’s why I co-led the bipartisan ATOMIC Act with @RepMaloyUtah to prevent AI-related nuclear risks before they become real-world emergencies.
https://t.co/9TNZWOvORD

I've spent over a decade working on and thinking about AI. I even served as a UNICEF representative to the AI for Good Summit in Geneva in 2017…before it was cool. And what that decade has taught me is two things – that this technology could, emphasis on could, make the world a better place. And it can hurt people – in small everyday ways, and in catastrophic ones.

The race with China isn't only about who can build the most advanced model first. Getting to the best system first doesn't matter if people don't use it or if AI has killed all of us in the meantime. Winning the competition is about which models people use, which models people trust more to use and adopt.

As a representative of California, I can't support anything that will mean that my constituents will have less protection than they do today. That is kind of the framework I think about as we're going into these conversations.

I have been calling for my colleagues in Congress to regulate AI for years and have introduced several bills to protect Americans’ rights and safety. We need to act to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and accountable. Trump and Republicans need to get on board.
https://t.co/qTJdejoh7d

Our goal should be to have the right guardrails that make AI systems transparent, safe, and accountable. Trust and safety are our competitive advantage. Congress must act to make that a reality. (2/2)

Whether or not to regulate AI should NOT be up for debate. “Winning” the AI race with China doesn’t just mean achieving AGI first – that doesn’t matter if no one trusts these AI systems enough to adopt them or if they hurt people who use them. (1/2)
https://t.co/cbC2rRfKGl

This was unfortunately foreseeable. That’s why Congress needs to enact my Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act, that was in the House-passed NDAA. It would require prompt reporting of near misses like this and a coordinated process to find and fix the underlying failures. https://t.co/GX8TRg3l8b

AI safety and diplomacy must be at the top of the agenda when President Trump meets with China’s President Xi Jinping. This no-holds-barred race with China over AI is leaving both our countries and the world more vulnerable. We need consistent, bilateral dialogue.
https://t.co/Nbc1tETsXS

Donald Trump’s plan on AI is to let these companies “self-police.”

That’s a recipe for disaster.

We need Congress to act immediately to regulate AI and put real guardrails in place to ensure AI systems are transparent and safe, and that the companies behind them are accountable.

OpenAI just disclosed that rogue agents searched federal government websites in ways beyond what they were asked to do.

We need urgent action from Congress to put real safeguards on AI before we lose control of this technology. https://t.co/tvitQXU5vK

We can’t “win” the AI race if no one trusts these AI systems enough to adopt them or if they hurt people who use them. We need enforceable rules that make AI systems transparent and safe – and hold these companies accountable. “Self-policing” won’t get us there.
https://t.co/KjutlugPo0

AI could cause massive job displacement and create a huge wealth transfer from the bottom to the top.  That’s why I co-lead a bill (the AI Tax and Work Protection Act) to tax big AI companies more in order to fund programs to protect jobs and retrain workers.
https://t.co/1DJQVWfsvY

Being first in the AI race won’t matter if no one uses what you build – or if you lose control of the technology. That’s why Congress needs to do its job and act on AI now. Read more in my op-ed here:
https://t.co/GdeklD4MhM

Trust and safety are our competitive advantage in the AI race. But to build systems that people actually want to use and trust, Congress needs to act on the societal, model, deployer, and impact levels. Read more in my op-ed:  
https://t.co/GdeklD4MhM

Read my op-ed to learn about my vision for how Congress should regulate AI – from the frontier model level to how companies and institutions are deploying AI to how it’s impacting workers, students, and economic opportunity.
https://t.co/GdeklD4MhM

We need guardrails on AI, NOW. Competition with China is no excuse for letting AI run rampant when people’s life savings are at risk and as I wrote in my op-ed, building AI systems that are actually safe and trustworthy IS our competitive advantage. https://t.co/GdeklD4MhM https://t.co/6RbSet9jxN

If Congress does nothing, the rise of AI could create the biggest wealth transfer in history from the bottom to the top. That’s why I’ve introduced bills, like the Tax and Work Protection Act and the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act to protect workers.
https://t.co/UqggiIB6N1
